discovery: Optical metamaterials and metasurfaces: engineering the electromagnetic response of matter through designed subwavelength structure
motivation: Pendry showed theoretically that artificial subwavelength structures can produce electromagnetic responses absent in nature, including magnetism at high frequencies, negative refraction and the perfect lens, and he founded transformation optics. Smith experimentally realised the first negative-index metamaterial (2000-2001) and the first electromagnetic cloak (2006), proving these ideas physically. Capasso reduced metamaterials to two dimensions: his generalized laws of reflection and refraction (2011) from phase-gradient metasurfaces led to flat metalenses and wavefront-shaping optics now moving into industrial manufacturing and consumer devices. Together their work changed optics from a science limited by available materials into one where light is controlled by designed nanostructure. This is now a central paradigm across photonics, from imaging and sensing to optical computing, light management in solar cells, and quantum optics. It joins deep electromagnetic insight with experimental elegance and wide technological reach.
